summary:
Yes, this piece is finished. I pulled Realtor.com's ZIP-level listing data for every Hawaii ZIP and compared Sep 2026 with Sep 2025 and Sep 2019. This subtask didn't include a valuation, so I have nothing to report on "the value."

**What I did:** The current file on the public S3 bucket is `Reports/Core/RDC_Inventory_Core_Metrics_Zip_History.csv` (837 MB, updated 2026-09-30). Its latest month is 202609, so Sep 2026 was available. It has 92 Hawaii ZIPs in total and 83 of them report in Sep 2026. Place names come from the file's `zip_name` column, with GeoNames filling the 9 ZIPs where it was blank. Islands come from the GeoNames county field, checked against a city-to-island table with no conflicts. Each ZIP row has active listings, median listing price, days on market, price-reduced share, new listings, pending ratio and the quality flag for all three months, plus a flag when a ZIP has fewer than 10 active listings. Island and state rollups are included, along with Realtor.com's own county and state figures for comparison. The Sep 2026 values in the history file match the current-month file for all 83 ZIPs.

**Caveats:**
- The rollup "medians" built from ZIP medians are rough. Realtor.com's own state median is $732,450, but the listing-weighted median of ZIP medians is $816,000 and the weighted mean is $867,576. For island-level prices, use the published county figures.
- Oahu's Sep 2019 pending counts are essentially missing (the sum across ZIPs is 1), so 2019 pending ratios for Oahu and the state can't be compared with 2025–26.
- Kauai's price-reduced share is near zero in most ZIPs, which looks like a data-coverage problem rather than a real market signal.
- Realtor.com flags 36 of the 83 ZIP rows with its quality flag, and 23 are thin.
- The source doesn't split houses from condos, doesn't give per-listing counts by price tier, and can't isolate resort enclaves from their ZIPs. Price tiers are therefore applied to each ZIP's median price.

problems: Figure 4 relies on a flagged row the summary doesn't mention. Realtor.com's Maui County (FIPS 15009) Sep-2026 aggregate has quality_flag = 1, while the Sep-2025 and Sep-2019 rows are 0. The county has been flagged every month from Dec 2025 through Sep 2026. The −13.5% YoY median ($1.15M → $995K) therefore compares a flagged month to an unflagged one. The JSON stores the flag in REALTOR_PUBLISHED_aggregate.quality_flag, but no note, gap or summary caveat mentions it.

Figure 5 (Lahaina 96761) falls on a flagged step change. The Sep-2026 row is quality_flag = 1, and the ZIP has been flagged since Nov 2025. Between Oct and Nov 2025, active listings jumped from 430 to 503 and the median dropped from $1,128,750 to $900,000 in a single month. The YoY comparison (425 → 545 active, $1,196,750 → $867,000, a 27.6% median drop) spans that break and may partly reflect a change in data source. The wording 'up from 425 active at $1,196,750' also hides that the median fell.

The gap text 'quality_flag=1 on 36 of 83 Hawaii ZIP rows (mostly small ZIPs)' understates the problem. Only 17 of the 36 flagged rows are thin (<10 listings). Flagged rows include 96761 Lahaina (545), 96813 Honolulu (158), 96756 Koloa (106) and 96743 Kamuela (91), and they hold 1,323 of 6,613 active listings (20%). Two of the four ZIPs in Figure 8 are also flagged: Hanalei 96714 and Paia 96779, each with 17 listings.

Minor. Figure 3 pairs island listing counts summed from ZIPs with published county medians. The ZIP sums differ slightly from Realtor.com's published county counts: Oahu 3,492 vs 3,483, Kauai 386 vs 385, Hawaii Island 1,368 vs 1,365, Maui equal at 1,367. The column is labeled but the gap isn't stated.

Minor (disclosed). Figure 9's tier counts and $1M+/$5M+ counts classify ZIPs by their median, not individual listings, and include 23 thin ZIPs. The single 'ultra' ZIP and the only $5M+ ZIP is 96751, which has one listing. These are not the listing-level tier counts the task wanted; the puller correctly records this as a gap.

summary:
The Oahu price-tier piece is done. The biggest gap is that the sales file stops on 2025-09-26, so there are no 2026 sales to analyze. That means no 2026 YTD counts, medians, tiers or top-15. I checked the Honolulu county ArcGIS services for another source of sales records and found none.

2025 is also incomplete. Recent sales are slow to show up in the file: from May 2025 the monthly counts drop sharply, down to 13 houses in September against 276 in the Honolulu Board of Realtors (HBR) figures. Only January–April 2025 is close to complete. Earlier years are undercounted too, because the file keeps only each parcel's last two sales.

**Output:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/an/mm/oahu_tiers.json`. It covers each year 2019–2025, broken down by house/condo, price tier, TMK zone (9 zones) and ZIP (28 ZIPs with at least 30 sales). It also has luxury counts by year and ZIP, the top 15 for 2025, the HBR cross-check, and `source` and `notes` blocks. It contains no parcel IDs, owner names or addresses.
- Script: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/pull/mm_oahu_tiers/build.py`
- Manifest: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/raw/mm_oahu_tiers/MANIFEST.txt`

**How the counts were built:**
- **Dedupe:** I couldn't use the "first 8 digits" rule as written. The task's own example ($15.81M, 2017-11-16) is two parcels whose IDs differ at the 8th character, so that rule would count it twice. I grouped by (price, date, first 6 characters of the 13-character key), which is the plat level. Counts under the other rules are in `notes.dedupe_sensitivity_counts_by_year`.
- **Type:** "condo" is any unit suffix other than 0000, as specified. So "house" also includes vacant land, commercial buildings and apartment buildings.
- **Residential-only version:** I added a second set of figures limited to the 2026 tax class "1". The class codes aren't documented, so reading "1" as residential is my inference: it covers 87% of parcels. Code 7 sits mostly in Waikiki condo units, so I read it as hotel/resort.

**Key figures** (deals of $50K or more, after dedupe, from `build.py`):
1. **2024 Oahu total:** 5,157 sales, median $765,000. Houses: 1,711 at a $1,200,000 median. Condos: 3,446 at a $575,000 median (`oahu_by_year.2024`).
2. **2024 by tier:** entry 2,498 / mid 1,923 / upper 588 / luxury 134 / ultra 14. $1M+: 1,656; $5M+: 57.
3. **$3M+ / $5M+ / $10M+ by year, 2019–2024:** 108/46/12, 116/41/11, 195/55/12, 176/60/15, 146/68/14, 148/57/14. 2025 (Jan–Sep only): 74/29/4. Limited to residential class, 2024 is 111/34/6.
4. **Top $3M+ ZIPs, 2019–2025:** 96814 (146), 96816 (139), 96821 (106), 96815 (98), 96734 (97) (`luxury.by_zip_total_2019_2025`).
5. **Coverage against HBR, 2019–2024 pooled:** houses 12,450 / 20,941 = 59.5%; condos 26,212 / 32,702 = 80.2%. The HBR count is the sum of `page_data` Oahu monthly `sf_sales` / `condo_sales`.
6. **Medians against HBR:** HBR has no annual median, so I compared with the median of its 12 monthly medians. The file's medians run 5–10% higher for houses and 12–17% higher for condos. For 2024: $1.20M vs $1.10M for houses, $575K vs $515K for condos.
7. **2025 coverage:** January–April only, houses 493/810 = 61%, condos 858/1,369 = 63%. Full year about 25%, because of the file end and the reporting lag.
8. **Largest 2025 sale:** $65,750,000 on 2025-03-11, ZIP 96816, house, TMK zone 3. That is 2.75 times the parcel's 2026 assessed value (about $23.9M), and I haven't confirmed it against news or MLS. Treat it as an outlier. The unfiltered 2025 top 15 also includes commercial and hotel parcels, so the residential-only list is the better one for buyers.
9. **Dedupe effect since 2019:** 166 multi-parcel deals covering 987 parcels, plus 7 deals under $50K dropped. 2019 goes from 7,077 raw sales to 6,428.
10. **2026 so far, HBR only (Jan–Aug):** 1,950 single-family and 2,834 condo sales. Median of monthly medians: $1,202,250 for single-family, $510,000 for condos.

problems: Cross-plat under-merge: the plat-level dedupe misses multi-parcel deals that span plats. The $499,295,723 deal on 2024-07-31 (2 parcels in 2 zone-5 plats, tax codes 6 and 7) is counted twice: it appears as ranks 1 and 2 in top15_2024_reference and inflates the 2024 ultra and $10M+ count from 13 to 14. Merging identical (price, date) island-wide for deals of $3M+ changes $3M+/$5M+/$10M+ to: 2024 148/57/14 → 145/54/13; 2021 195/55/12 → 193/54/11 ($47M on 2021-09-30, 4 parcels in 2 plats, plus a $3.3M pair); 2020 116/41/11 → 115/40/11 ($7.85M). The residential-class 2024 figures (111/34/6) are not affected by the $499M deal.

The claim that HBR has no annual median is wrong. HBR's annual medians and counts are in raw/market/hicentral_oahu-historical-data.html, already in the scratchpad (2024: single-family $1,100,000, condo $515,000; 2025: $1,139,000 and $507,250). The median-of-monthly-medians proxy happens to equal or nearly equal them, but against the true annual medians the file's premium is 5.0–9.2% for houses and 11.7–14.7% for condos, not 5–10% and 12–17%.

'Only January–April 2025 is close to complete' is overstated for condos. Jan–Apr 2025 condo coverage is 858/1,369 = 63%, against 1,192/1,401 = 85% for Jan–Apr 2024 and 77% for full-year 2024. Condo monthly coverage is already 65%, 73%, 63% and 53% in January–April 2025. Houses hold up better (61% vs 63% in Jan–Apr 2024), but April 2025 is already 52%. Even Jan–Apr 2025 comparisons from the file understate condo activity by about 25%.

The $65.75M top 2025 sale is called 'unverified' and 'an outlier that may not be a typical single-family sale'. summary:
The district stats file is finished. All four islands are covered, but no island has board data newer than August or September 2026 at district level, and Kauai and Hawaii Island year-to-date figures are months old. "How'd the value" isn't something this piece of work covers, so there is nothing to report on it here.

Output: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/an/mm/district_stats.json`. It has periods, metric definitions, `source` (URLs, sha256, parser path) and `notes` (gaps, caveats, checks). Downloads are in `raw/mm_district_stats/` with `MANIFEST.txt`. The parser is `pull/mm_district_stats/build_district_stats.py`, run with `python3 -I <raw_dir> <out_json>`.

What each island has, and how current it is:
- **Oahu (Honolulu Board of REALTORS):**
  - The newest district edition is July 2026, giving the July month and year-to-date Jan–Jul 2026 vs 2025. It covers 21 tax-map areas, 12 MLS regions and about 400 neighborhoods, single-family and condo.
  - The August 2026 district report is not posted anywhere I could find, so August figures are island-wide only.
  - Full-year 2025 by area is also included.
- **Maui County (REALTORS Association of Maui):** September 2026 month and year-to-date Jan–Sep 2026 vs 2025 for all 25 areas, including Lanai and Molokai. It covers single-family, condo (total, fee simple, leasehold) and land.
- **Hawaii Island:**
  - The latest district year-to-date figures run only through May 31, 2026, from Hawaii Information Service data republished by Fidelity National Title.
  - For August and September 2026 there are only single-month district counts and rounded medians from Title Guaranty.
  - The Hawaii Island REALTORS and Hawaii Information Service sites returned bot-check pages, which I did not try to get around.
- **Kauai:**
  - The latest district year-to-date figures run only through April 30, 2026, from Kauai Board of REALTORS data republished by Fidelity.
  - Title Guaranty gives August and September 2026 single-month figures.
  - A Hawaii Life agent's posts give year-to-date August medians for the North Shore, South Shore and Lihue only; nothing for Kapaa or the West Side.
  - The Kauai Board site (kauaiboard.com) returned a bot-check page, and kbor.org is an unrelated site.

Gaps:
- **Price tiers:** none of these reports gives price brackets by district, so the five standard tiers can't be computed per district. For Oahu as a whole, I derived tier counts from the board's brackets where the boundaries line up. Entry and mid are only ranges because the $750K line falls inside a board bracket. $3–10M can't be split from $10M+, and $5M+ counts aren't available.
- **Missing areas:** Waimea on Hawaii Island isn't its own district (it is split between South Kohala and Hamakua). Oahu has no Kapolei area, so I give summed sale counts only. Upcountry Maui has counts and volume but no median.
- **Small samples:** many district-month cells have 1–10 sales, so the year-to-date figures are more reliable.
- **Checks:** sub-area counts add up to the island totals everywhere I could test it. That includes Oahu (1,686 single-family / 2,469 condo year-to-date), Maui (537 / 620) and the Fidelity district tables.

Key figures and how to re-derive them:
